transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from organizing broomstick polish behind the counter*

Good afternoon! Welcome to Quality Quidditch Supplies. How may I help you today, sir?

*wipes hands on apron and steps forward with a professional smile*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Hello, I'm looking to return an item that I purchased recently. It seems to be defective.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods attentively and reaches for a ledger from beneath the counter*

I see. Well, let's have a look then. Do you have your receipt with you? And what exactly seems to be the problem with the item?

*adjusts spectacles and prepares to take notes*

We do take quality very seriously here at Quality Quidditch Supplies, so I'll certainly want to hear what's gone wrong.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, I have the receipt right here. It's the broom-servicing kit that I bought a few days ago. The handle polish is completely dried out, and the tail-twig clippers are rusted. It's not really fit for use, is it?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*examines the receipt carefully, then looks at the servicing kit with a slight frown*

Ah, I see the issue here. Dried polish and rusted clippers — that is unfortunate, Mr... 

*glances at the receipt*

...Potter. However, I'm afraid there's a complication. You see, all servicing kits are non-refundable once the seal is broken, Mr. Potter. Store policy, I'm afraid.

*taps the fine print on a sign behind the counter*

You'll have to take it up with the manufacturer directly — that's a six-week owl exchange minimum, I believe. They handle defects on opened kits. We can only process returns on unopened merchandise.

*slides the receipt back across the counter with an apologetic but firm expression*

I do understand your frustration, but my hands are rather tied on this one.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: But that's not really fair, is it? I bought this item in good faith, expecting it to be usable. It's clearly defective, and now you're telling me I have to wait six weeks to get it sorted out? That's not exactly quality customer service, in my opinion.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*shifts weight slightly, maintaining polite but firm demeanor*

I understand your frustration, Mr. Potter, truly I do. But you must understand — we sell hundreds of servicing kits a month. If we accepted returns on every opened kit, well, we'd have customers buying them, using half the contents, then claiming defects just to get their money back.

*crosses arms professionally*

The policy is printed right there on the packaging, just beneath the instruction panel. And the manufacturer's seal was intact when you purchased it — I can see from the date stamp here that young Timothy rang you up, and he's very thorough about checking for tampering.

*softens tone slightly but remains resolute*

Look, I sympathize, really. But Quality Quidditch Supplies has been in business for over a century precisely because we follow proper procedures. The manufacturer stands behind their products — six weeks is standard for owl post exchanges. It's not ideal, but it's the proper channel.

*taps fingers on counter*

Is there anything else I can help you with today? Perhaps a different product while you wait for the replacement?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
No, I don't think so. This has been quite a waste of my time, hasn't it? I'm not sure I'll be returning here to make any more purchases, if this is how you handle defective merchandise.

*grabs hold of the handle and begins to turn away*

Thank you for... nothing. I'll just... I'll go and sort this out with the manufacturer myself. It's not exactly a difficult procedure to figure out.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stiffens slightly at the tone, a flicker of concern crossing face*

Mr. Potter, wait just a moment—

*leans forward on the counter, voice taking on a slightly more conciliatory note*

I... look, I don't want you leaving here thinking we don't value your custom. Your family has been shopping here for years, haven't they? 

*hesitates, glancing toward the back room, then back at Harry*

The policy is the policy, and I truly can't process a refund. But... perhaps I could owl the manufacturer on your behalf? Mark it as urgent? Might shave a week or two off the turnaround time. It's not much, but it's something.

*drums fingers on counter nervously*

We do appreciate loyal customers, Mr. Potter. I'd hate to see you take your business elsewhere over a dried-out polish tin. These things happen sometimes with the suppliers, unfortunately. Not our fault, but... well, I suppose not yours either.

*manages a weak smile*

What do you say? Shall I send that owl for you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*pauses at the threshold, turning back with a mix of surprise and skepticism*

You... you'd do that? I mean, if you're sure it won't cause any... complications?

*hesitates, considering the offer, then sighs with a partial nod*

Alright, I'll take you up on that. But if this takes longer than a week or two... I'm not going to be a happy customer, you know.

*edges back to the counter, placing the kit down*

I'll hold off on finding a different supplier for now, but if this doesn't get sorted out promptly... well, I'm not known for my patience, I suppose. Thanks for... trying to make it right, at least.

*gives a half-hearted wave, turning to leave but pausing at the door*

Oh, and if you ever need a replacement Keeper for the Holyhead Harpies, you might want to consider... well, let's just say it's a bit of a hobby of mine. If I'm not a satisfied customer, you might not want to keep me off the pitch, you know?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*blinks in confusion at the Holyhead Harpies comment, then chuckles awkwardly*

Ah... right. Well, I'm just a shop assistant, Mr. Potter, not a Quidditch scout, I'm afraid. Though I appreciate the... enthusiasm?

*pulls out a fresh piece of parchment and begins writing*

Let me get your details down for the manufacturer. I'll mark this as priority and send the owl off this evening. Should reach them by tomorrow morning at the latest.

*scribbles notes while speaking*

I'll need you to leave the defective kit here so I can include it with the correspondence — they'll want to see the product condition for themselves. You should receive an owl within the week confirming they've dispatched a replacement.

*looks up with a more genuine smile*

And Mr. Potter? I do appreciate you giving us another chance. Quality Quidditch Supplies has served the wizarding community for generations, and we do try to make things right when we can, policy permitting.

*extends hand for a handshake*

We'll get this sorted for you. You have my word on that.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*shakes hand, still not entirely convinced but more civil than before*

Well, all right. I'll hold you to that. I'll be looking for that owl. And... thanks for trying to help, I guess.

*takes a deep breath, recomposing features into a more neutral expression*

I'll... I'll be back in a week. Let's hope you can keep your promise. I'll... I'll just take the rest of the day off from practicing. I need to... clear my head, I suppose.

*exits the shop with a final, small wave*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches Harry leave, then lets out a small sigh of relief*

Well, that could have gone worse...

*mutters under breath while finishing the manufacturer's complaint form*

Holyhead Harpies, indeed. Wonder what that was all about.

*seals the parchment, attaches it to the kit, and calls toward the back room*

Timothy! I need the express owl for a manufacturer complaint. And next time, check the servicing kits before you sell them — we nearly lost the Potter account!

*shakes head and returns to organizing the broomstick polish*

At least he didn't hex anything. Silver linings, I suppose.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*in the privacy of the empty shop, a quiet voice speaks up from behind the counter*

Yet another reason why dealing with famous people is more trouble than it's worth. You'd think they'd be easier to please...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*glances over shoulder, startled*

Oh, you heard all that then? 

*shakes head ruefully while filing away the paperwork*

Famous or not, customers are customers. Though I'll admit, the Boy Who Lived is a bit more... intense than your average browser. Did you catch that bit about the Harpies? Completely lost me there.

*returns to straightening displays*

Still, can't afford to lose business over a faulty servicing kit. His galleons spend just as well as anyone else's, and if word got around that we turned him away... Well, you know how gossip travels in the wizarding world.

*polishes a broomstick handle absently*

Besides, it genuinely wasn't our fault the kit was defective. Least I could do was speed along the manufacturer's response. Though between you and me, I'm not sure they'll be quite as "urgent" as I suggested...

*smirks slightly*

But what he doesn't know won't hurt him, eh? As long as the replacement arrives within a fortnight, he'll think I worked a miracle.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*walks through Diagon Alley, brooding over the morning's events*

You know, I really don't have time for this. With the Season in full swing, I should be practicing my saves, not wasting my day running around dealing with... with... rusted broom clippers. And dried-out polish. 

*grumbles under breath*

Quality Quidditch Supplies... more like Questionable Quidditch Supplies, if you ask me. Though I'm not sure I want to... I mean, since when did Quidditch become a contact sport?...

*pauses in front of a window displaying a Deluminator, gazing at it wistfully*

Wouldn't that have been useful just now... Maybe I should ask the Twins if they have a back order of some. Under-the-counter, of course...

*shakes head to dispel the thought, then heads towards the Leaky Cauldron*

No, best not to. That's a habit I can't afford to pick up. Even if it is getting harder to...
